test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements regarding the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan launched in 2024 is/are correct?

1. The scheme aims for the holistic development of tribal areas through 25 interventions in health, education and livelihood.

2. The scheme benefits only 10 states with scheduled areas, excluding other tribal areas.

3. It was launched by Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar in Jharkhand on 2ⁿd October 2024.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan** was launched in 2024 to ensure the holistic development of tribal areas.
 
• The scheme focuses on **25 interventions** spanning health, education, and livelihood to improve the quality of life for tribal populations.
 
• It aims to address socio-economic disparities and promote sustainable development in tribal areas.
 
• Unlike the statement in Option 2, the scheme is not limited to only 10 states with scheduled areas. It encompasses a broader range of tribal regions.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect as the scheme was launched by another dignitary, not Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar, and the launch details provided in the statement are inaccurate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tribal Development:**

 
 
• Tribal communities in India face challenges like inadequate access to education, healthcare, and sustainable livelihoods.
 
• Government schemes aim to bridge these gaps and ensure inclusive growth for tribal populations.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Areas:**
 
 
• Scheduled Areas are regions identified under the Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution to protect tribal communities.
 
• These areas receive special administration and developmental support.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP):**
 
 
• The TSP strategy ensures that a fixed proportion of funds are allocated for tribal development under various central and state government schemes.
 
• It aims to address the socio-economic gaps in tribal regions.
 
 
 
• **Jharkhand and Tribal Focus:**
 
 
• Jharkhand is home to a significant tribal population and has been a focal point for tribal development initiatives.
 
• Efforts in the state include improving education, healthcare access, and preservation of tribal culture.
